steps.text: Place eggs in a saucepan and cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until hard-cooked, 10 to 12 minutes. Drain and cool in an ice bath. Once cool, peel hard boiled eggs. Slice eggs in half lengthwise and scoop out yolks.
Mash yolks with vinegar, mayonnaise, mustard, salt, and pepper until smooth. You may need to add more mayonnaise to hold the mixture together, but it should be slightly dry.
Carefully put egg yolk mixture back into egg whites but do not pack it. There will be enough mixture so the whites are overfilled. Sprinkle with paprika. Refrigerate until ready to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Traditional Deviled Eggs
raw_recipe.description: Delicious deviled eggs made with perfectly cooked hard-boiled eggs and an easy mayonnaise and mustard filling for a classic holiday appetizer.
raw_recipe.name: Traditional Deviled Eggs

review.reviewBody: These were excellent and easy to make!!! If using fresh eggs, put lots of salt in the boiling water to make it easier to remove the shells.
Great recipe. But boiling eggs for 10-15 minutes will make the yolk grey. Cook for 6 minutes after the water begins to boil for perfectly hard, bright yellow yolks.

The best way to make easy-to-peel hard-boiled eggs with pure yellow centers is to place the eggs in a pot of cold water and add a teaspoon of salt. Place the pot on the stove and bring to a boil. Cover the pot and remove from heat and let sit for 13 minutes. Drain the eggs and immediately place in an ice bath until completely cooled. Drain and enjoy your perfectly cooked hard-boiled eggs. Works every time and no ugly green yolk.
Add about 1/4 of cheddar cheese, 2 tbsps of cream cheese and a pinch of hot pepper and see what this does to this recipe... truly kicks it up a few notches.

Doubled all of the seasonings and saved the paprika for the top of the eggs. I added an extra yolk. I put the yolk mixture in a ziplock bag overnight and piped into the eggs the next morning and sprinkled with paprika, delicious!

Pretty good deviled eggs. It needed much more mayonnaise to get it still "dry" but creamy. These were okay, but something was missing in the flavor. Maybe more vinegar or mustard? I have another one here by Margaret Sanders that I prefer, but this is a nice standard base to start with.

Half of the family likes sweet deviled eggs and half likes them tart so instead of vinegar I use bread & butter pickle juice in half of the egg mixture and dill pickle juice in the other half. Everyone is happy then until we run out!

This is an easy recipe. I used only 1 hard-boiled egg, since I was the only person in my home celebrating National Deviled Egg Day. So, the other ingredients were basically a dash of this and a pinch of that. My changes were: garlic-flavored wine vinegar, chopped yellow onion, onion powder, spicy brown mustard and chopped chives for garnish. My husband said the filling was a bit vinegary but not bad.

I increased the mayo to 2 Tblsps and the mustard ( use Dijon) to a generous full half teaspoon . Kept vinegar measurement the same but made it half teaspoon each of White vinegar and half cider vinegar . Made all the difference! Added a few drops hot sauce too. Very good! Will definitely keep this one.

These are o good! Just made them for Thanksgving tomorrow. The recipe didn't specify which mustard or vinegar so I used rice wine vinegar & Dijon Mustard & put just a pinch of celery seed in with the mix! Has great traditional flavor! I had to restrain myself from eating more than 1.

I like to add dried dill weed to the yolk mixture and a sprinkle of sugar to add a bit of sweetness without adding extra liquid. I also sprinkle the finished filled egg with the paprika instead of adding to the yolk mixture. This is a great basic recipe to make it your own.
I put in relish too.

70 yo bachelor who usually cooks well here. Haven't cooked hard boiled eggs in a while! Not sure what I did wrong, other than forgetting the salt in the water. Left the eggs on the boil for an extra minute... let them sit and extra 2 minutes and they were still under cooked! Yolks barely cooked...whites way too soft! Only managed to peal 3 successfully!! Please help as I love deviled eggs!
Worst recipe I’ve found online. And I make deviled eggs often. Just not the right consistency and very bland flavor. Not enough of each ingredient.

I would have rated this 4, but I had to double all the ingredients to make this smooth. I also added a ~ teaspoon of my zucchini relish to give it more flavor. This made it delicious! This is the first time I've ever made deviled eggs and I'm glad I tried it because it's pretty easy.
LOVED THE RECIPE, ADDED A LITTLE OREGANO. GRAND DAUGHTER LOVED THEM TO.

needs to be about THREE tablespoons mayonnaise and a teaspoon of mustard..I had to add to the recipe. I thought I was using the clasic deviled egg recipe that I like on the internet, but this is obviously not that one
This recipe is great, have made it many times and my friends loved it.
Needs more vinegar and mustard.
I used Costco eggs. I had to adjust the mayo, mustard and vinegar 4X to get the yolk mixture to not be soooooo stiff!
